subject: Reserved capacity commit: tenor & GPU-cost sensitivity
messages:
From: Sam Park <sam@acme.ai>
To: Olga Petrov <olga@redwood.ai>
Cc: Procurement Team <procurement@acme.ai>
Date: Sun, 12 Apr 2026 15:08:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Reserved capacity ask — sizing & pricing sensitivity

Hi Olga,

Thanks for the demo — the latency and cost numbers look promising. Procurement asked we share a few scenarios so they can evaluate risk against GPU market moves. I attached an initial forecast (acme_commit_scenarios.xlsx) with three demand profiles through Q4 and a suggested 12‑ vs 24‑month tenor.

Key asks from our side:
- Can Redwood provide a pricing sensitivity matrix if GPU input costs change by ±20% and ±40%?
- If GPU market spikes, what internal approval path exists for ad hoc credits or temporary discounts?
- Is there an option to stage the commit (phased activation) to reduce upfront exposure?

Procurement would like a one‑page summary for their supplier committee by end of next week. Can you get back with a short memo plus any internal escalation criteria?

Thanks,
Sam Park
Head of Platform Partnerships
Acme AI

[Attachment: acme_commit_scenarios.xlsx (spreadsheet)]

From: Olga Petrov <olga@redwood.ai>
To: Sam Park <sam@acme.ai>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 14 Apr 2026 09:34:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Reserved capacity ask — sizing & pricing sensitivity

Sam — really appreciate the detail in the scenarios. High level response below; I'll get a short memo and a decision tree to you by Friday.

Quick answers (summary):
- Sensitivity: We can model price pass‑through triggers tied to an industry GPU index (monthly). We typically show impact at ±15%, ±30%, ±50% on per‑token cost and committed revenue. I will attach the matrix.
- Credits/discounts: For one‑off market shocks, approvals are tiered: SDR/AE concessions < $25k handled by Sales Ops; discounts up to 15% require Sales Director sign‑off; >15% or credits impacting GAAP revenue require Finance (Laura) and Revenue Ops sign‑off and occasionally SVP Sales escalation.
- Phased activation: Yes — we offer phased ramp with an activation schedule in the SOW (e.g., 40/30/30 over three quarters) plus a 'soft floor' pricing if utilization drops.

Open items for us to model:
1) Desired minimum committed throughput per quarter.
2) Preferred tenor (12 vs 24 months) and any optional extension triggers.
3) Whether Acme wants an indexation clause tied to a third‑party market index or a fixed schedule.

I'll draft a concise memo with a recommended negotiation posture (we'll include a conservative midline pricing and a fallback discount ladder) and circulate internally. Looping in Karthik and Ben to flag anything I missed on fleet sizing or finance gating.

—Olga
Head of Strategic Deals, Redwood Inference
[Attachment: proposed_malpais_term_sheet_v1.pdf (term sheet stub)]

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.ai>
To: Olga Petrov <olga@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben@redwood.ai>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 15 Apr 2026 11:02:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Reserved capacity ask — sizing & pricing sensitivity

Olga — quick internal notes on sizing/operational risk: 

1) Fleet allocation: If Acme chooses 24 months with phased activation, we should propose a soft allocation buffer (~10% above committed peak) to preserve latency targets without over‑provisioning. That gives operations a runway for hardware substitutions.
2) GPU cost shock handling: Recommend we offer two levers — (A) indexation with a quarterly reconciliation and (B) cap-and-collar on unit price (e.g., unit price adjusts but limited to ±25% per annum). The reconciliation should allow us to avoid retroactive credits beyond a defined quarterly window.
3) Approval path & escrow: For discounts impacting revenue recognition, we need a documented approval checklist (Finance signoff, legal, CRO). Ben — can you confirm whether Sales Ops has a precedent for temporary credit lines to cover market spikes?

I don't want to over‑expose our fleet. If negotiation moves to wider discounts (>20%), we should propose a blended approach: reduced committed throughput + a market‑indexed credit that amortizes over the tenor.

-Karthik
Director, Dedicated Capacity Planning

Date: Sat, 18 Apr 2026 09:22:00 -07:00
Subject: Reserved capacity commit — short memo & next steps

Sam / Procurement team — attaching the short memo and proposed term sheet (see links). Summary and next steps below.

Executive summary:
- Options modeled: 12‑month firm commit, 24‑month phased commit, and 24‑month blended with staged activation. We modeled GPU input cost shocks at ±20% and ±40%. The per‑token price sensitivity and net revenue impact are in the memo.
- Recommended commercial posture: 24‑month phased commit (40/35/25) with an indexation clause tied to a public GPU index, capped at ±30% annual movement and a quarterly reconciliation window. This reduces Acme's short‑term price exposure while giving Redwood predictable utilization to justify dedicated capacity.
- Discount & approval ladder: Temporary credits for market shocks handled by Sales Ops up to $25k. Discounts up to 15% require Sales Director. Anything exceeding 15% or with material GAAP impact requires Finance (Laura) and Revenue Ops. We propose a two‑week SLA for internal escalation decisions during negotiations.

Action items:
1) Acme to confirm preferred tenor and phased activation schedule by 2026‑04‑23.
2) Redwood will deliver a single‑page sensitivity matrix + term sheet redline by 2026‑04‑20. (Links attached)
3) If Acme requests >15% list discount, Redwood will provide a formal approval request packet for Finance review (expected 3 business days).

Attachments / links: proposed_malpais_term_sheet_v1.pdf, acme_commit_scenarios.xlsx, https://redwood.atlassian.net/browse/FIN-1234

If this looks good I can open a DocuSign pre‑fill and target a legal review window next week.

Thanks,
Olga Petrov
